_README: Explicit, versioned waivers for scripts/check-docs-parity.mjs.
A docs-site page that exists in English and NOT in a published locale is a finding.
This file is the ONLY way to declare that a page is deliberately not translated.
There is no silent exemption, and there is no blanket mute: a waiver that stops
suppressing anything (the page got translated, or its English source was renamed)
becomes a `waiver-stale` finding, so dead entries surface instead of accumulating.
Schema, per entry — every field below is REQUIRED except `expires`:
path     page path relative to docs-site/src/content/docs, POSIX separators, NFC,
already canonical (no `./`, no `//`, no `..` segment, no backslashes), and
carrying a real page extension — e.g.
"explanation/security/threat-model.md".
Matching is by ROUTE (the same one Astro publishes), so one waiver covers
the page whether it is authored as .md or .mdx. A path with a made-up
extension is rejected rather than silently resolving to a real route.
locales  an array of locale codes that must appear in docs-site/src/site-locales.mjs.
`"*"` is REJECTED: it would expand from whatever locale list exists at run
time, so a waiver granted today would silently mute a locale added next
year — an exemption nobody reviewed. Name the locales you are exempting.
reason   at least 20 characters saying WHY this page is not translated. "n/a",
"todo" and "later" are rejected by length on purpose — a waiver with no
argument behind it is the thing this mechanism exists to prevent. No
program can judge whether prose is a GOOD reason, so review still applies.
date     real ISO YYYY-MM-DD calendar date, not in the future. `2026-13-45` has the
shape of a date and is rejected.
expires  OPTIONAL real ISO YYYY-MM-DD date, must be AFTER `date`. Past that date the
waiver stops suppressing and reports `waiver-expired`. Prefer an expiry for
anything not permanent; an open-ended waiver is a permanent hole.
Two entries covering the same (locale, route) are rejected as duplicates: otherwise
both would count as used and neither could ever be reported stale.
NOT waivable here, because they are excluded structurally instead:
* archived version snapshots (the `VERSIONS` slugs in docs-site/src/site-locales.mjs,
e.g. 2026-06/) are English-authored point-in-time archives BY DESIGN and are
skipped by the checker — under the root AND under each locale, because
starlight-versions copies every locale when it cuts a snapshot.
* `orphan` findings (a translated page with no English source) — that is a broken
tree, not a translation policy decision. Delete or re-point the page.
* `format-drift` (both sides exist for one route, in different source formats) —
it is reported as a NOTE and never fails the gate, so there is nothing to waive.
* `route-collision` (two source files resolving to one published route) — a site
defect; rename one.
